newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian central bank says three banks sold.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian central bank says three banks sold.

text.p: The Nigerian central bank said on Tuesday it had found buyers for three commercial banks it offered for sale last year.
Central bank governor Paul Ogwuma told reporters that National Bank, New Nigerian Bank and African Continental Bank had been sold.
He did not name the new owners nor the amount paid but said 1.7 billion naira would be required to reactivate them.
The three are among state-owned banks run aground by bad debts and corruption.
The central bank has taken over several distressed banks since the military government decided to arrest the trend in the country's financial sector and advertised them for sale.
"There should be no more distress in the banks. We want to have a virile banking sector," Ogwuma said.
Under new government requirements, banks have until the end of next year to raise their capital base to a minimum of 500 million naira, a nine-fold increase, or be liquidated.

So-called distressed banks have an even shorter deadline -- March 31 1997 -- to recapitalise to the new level or be liquidated, a measure that industry analysts say suggests that the government wants the troubled banks to die.
